Bug_Title: "Serializable" inner classes of non-serializable outer classes should be "static"
Bug_Details:
Non-static inner classes contain a reference to an instance of the outer class. Hence, serializing a non-static inner class will result in an
attempt at serializing the outer class as well. If the outer class is not serializable, serialization will fail, resulting in a runtime error.
Making the inner class static (i.e., "nested") avoids this problem, as no reference to an instance of the outer class is required.
Serializing the inner class can be done independently of the outer class. Hence, inner classes implementing Serializable should be static if the outer class does not implement Serializable .
Be aware of the semantic differences between an inner class and a nested one:
an inner class can only be instantiated within the context of an instance of the outer class. a nested ( static ) class can be instantiated independently of the outer class.
an inner class can only be instantiated within the context of an instance of the outer class.

Bug_Explanation: The InnerClass implements Serializable but is a non-static inner class of the OuterClass, which is not serializable. This means serialization of InnerClass will attempt to serialize OuterClass as well, resulting in a runtime error.
Trigger_Explanation: The test case calls the showBug method that attempts to serialize the non-static inner class InnerClass of the non-serializable OuterClass, thereby causing an exception and making the test fail.
